statement_record.book: If Q has all meets and P is any preorder, a monotone g : Q → P preserves meets IFF g is a right adjoint (has a left adjoint); dually, if P has all joins, a monotone f : P → Q preserves joins IFF f is a left adjoint. The 'only if' half is Prop 1.111; the converse builds the left adjoint by the numbered display (1.116), f(p) := ⋀{q ∈ Q | p ≤ g(q)}, whose monotonicity is Prop 1.91 and whose unit/counit come from meet-preservation and Prop 1.91, concluded by Prop 1.107.

statement_record.strength_comparison: both directions exist categorically, but the hard direction is intree-weaker for THIS item: GAFT carries an extra `SolutionSet U d` hypothesis at every d, which the book's preorder theorem does not need (for a complete preorder the meet of display (1.116) is itself a one-element solution set, so the hypothesis is vacuous there — but nothing in-tree discharges it). It is also stated over `Complete C` (limits of all small diagrams) and `PreservesImageLimit` (cone-level preservation), not over 'has all meets' / 'preserves meets', and it constructs the adjoint by Freyd's product+equalizer route (Theory/WeaklyInitial.v), not by the explicit formula (1.116). The easy direction (RAPL/LAPC) is intree-stronger than Prop 1.111 in generality — arbitrary diagram shapes in arbitrary categories, of which binary/subset meets are the thin-category instance.

gap: The preorder statement is never obtained. statement_record.book: For a function f : A → B, the preimage map f* : P(B) → P(A), B' ↦ f⁻¹(B'), is monotone and has BOTH a left adjoint, the direct image f_!(A') = {b | ∃ a ∈ A', f(a) = b}, and a right adjoint, the dual image f_*(A') = {b | ∀ a, f(a) = b → a ∈ A'}; so f_! ⊣ f* ⊣ f_*, all three induced automatically by f.
statement_record.intree: Program Definition Sub : C^op ⟶ Sets with fmap f := sub_reindex (unop f) : SubObj x → SubObj y (the chosen-pullback preimage of subobjects, with sub_reindex_id and sub_reindex_comp); plus, in Sets only, Sets_Image_Factorization : Factorization f EpiClass MonoClass factoring a map through Sets_Image = {b : Y & ∃ a : X, f a ≈ b}; plus the subobject preorder sub_le with sub_equiv_iff_mutual : (u ≈ v) ↔ (sub_le u v * sub_le v u).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: exactly ONE of the three maps exists, and none of the adjointness. `sub_reindex` is a faithful, indeed more general, f* (subobjects of an arbitrary category by pullback rather than subsets of a set), but `Sub` lands in Sets — it is functorial for ≈ only, and monotonicity of f* for `sub_le` is nowhere stated (`sub_reindex_respects` is respect for the setoid, not for the order). The direct image exists only as the image of a WHOLE map (`Sets_Image`), never as an operation SubObj A → SubObj B, and there is no dual image at any level. Neither of the book's two biconditionals (f_!(A') ⊆ B' ⟺ A' ⊆ f*(B') and f*(B') ⊆ A' ⟺ B' ⊆ f_*(A')) appears in any form.

statement_record.book: Given a Galois connection f : P → Q left adjoint to g : Q → P, the composite (f ; g) : P → P is a monotone endomap with p ≤ (f ; g)(p) for all p and (f ; g ; f ; g)(p) ≅ (f ; g)(p) — i.e. a closure operator (Def 1.120). Footnote 8: dually (g ; f) : Q → Q satisfies (g ; f)(q) ≤ q and idempotence up to ≅, an INTERIOR operator.
statement_record.intree: Theorem Adjunction_Monad : F ⊣ U → @Monad D (U ◯ F), whose class fields are ret {x} : x ~> M x, join {x} : M (M x) ~> M x, join_fmap_ret {x} : join ∘ fmap ret ≈ id, join_ret {x} : join ∘ ret (M x) ≈ id (Theory/Monad.v:92-109); the unit itself is Definition unit {x : D} : x ~> U (F x) := ⌊id⌋; invertibility of join is the SEPARATE Class IdempotentMonad := { idem_join_iso {x} : IsIsomorphism (@join C M _ x) }; the dual composite is Definition Adjunction_Comonad (A : F ⊣ U) : @Comonad C (F ◯ U).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger on clause (a) and on generality, intree-weaker on clause (b). Clause (a), p ≤ (f;g)(p), is exactly `unit`/`ret` and holds for every adjunction between arbitrary categories; monotonicity of the composite is functoriality of U ◯ F. Clause (b) is only half-present: a general monad supplies BOTH comparison arrows (join : M M x ~> M x and ret (M x) : M x ~> M M x) and the equations join ∘ ret(M x) ≈ id, join ∘ fmap ret ≈ id, but their being an ISOMORPHISM is false for a general monad and is imposed in-tree as the extra `IdempotentMonad` axiom. In a thin category (a preorder) invertibility is automatic because all parallel morphisms are equal — that step is nowhere taken in-tree.

gap: No order-theoretic instance and no closure-operator statement. Specifically: (i) there is no Galois connection in-tree (7sketches:1.4.1:def95: `GaloisConnection` has 0 hits and no functor between two `Proset`s is ever built), so the hypothesis of the construction cannot be written; (ii) `closure operator` occurs only as prose in Instance/Poset.v:48,64-68 — no definition, so the conclusion cannot be written either (see 7sketches:1.4.4:def120); (iii) the idempotence clause (b) is available only by ASSUMING `IdempotentMonad`, and nothing in-tree proves that a monad on a thin category is idempotent (grep 'thin' finds only comments), which is precisely the step that makes the book's claim automatic; (iv) the footnote-8 interior operator likewise exists only as `Adjunction_Comonad` — the dual inequality (g;f)(q) ≤ q is the comonad's `extract`, but no 'interior operator' statement or order instance exists.

statement_record.book: A CLOSURE OPERATOR on a preorder P is a monotone map j : P → P such that for all p ∈ P: (a) p ≤ j(p), and (b) j(j(p)) ≅ j(p) — idempotence only up to the preorder's induced isomorphism, not equality.

statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger as a categorification, never specialized. Instantiated at `Proset P` a `Monad` IS Def 1.120: the endofunctor is a monotone map, `ret` is clause (a), `join` together with `ret (M x)` gives clause (b)'s two comparisons, and all seven laws hold vacuously because Proset's hom-setoid identifies parallel proofs (`equiv := fun _ _ => True`).
